07 sections 6.14/6.15; list traced without scoring.; Source wording: A cell C is a tuple C = (M, pi, tau, G, I_in, I_out, {C_k}_k, Lambda): M is the cell's model type (spiking, LTC, SSM, ...), pi its precision profile (one format per tensor role), tau its native timescale and clock policy, G its geometric embedding, I its typed input/output ports, {C_k} its child cells (possibly empty), and Lambda its ledger: the observability record every cell must emit.

07 sections 6.14/6.15; list traced without scoring.; Source wording: Micro (units and motifs). Individual neurons, synapses and small motifs of 1–100 units: a spiking neuron with STDP, an LTC cell, a ternary perceptron, a Clifford rotor unit, a fractional-order integrator. The micro level is where most parameters live, so it is where low precision pays the most.

07 sections 6.14/6.15; list traced without scoring.; Source wording: Meso (circuits and organs). Circuits of 10^2–10^5 units that perform one function: a central pattern generator, a reservoir 'retina', a Mamba-style sequence summariser, a Hopfield episodic store, a homeostatic integrator. Each meso cell has one dominant model type and a precision profile.

07 sections 6.14/6.15; list traced without scoring.; Source wording: Macro (the organism and its society). The whole brain: arbitration, global neuromodulation, the world model, the body schema, and (optionally) the links between organisms in a population. The macro level holds few parameters but long-lived, error-intolerant state, so it often warrants the highest precision.

07 sections 6.14/6.15; list traced without scoring.; Source wording: Levels are relative, not absolute: a meso cell may itself be a complete NESTOR brain (brains within brains), and an entire organism may be one micro cell in a colony-level brain.

07 sections 6.14/6.15; list traced without scoring.; Source wording: Why nested: an A-Life organism has to do many different things on many different timescales at once: reflexes in milliseconds, locomotion rhythms in tenths of a second, foraging plans over minutes, homeostasis and 'mood' over hours, development and learning over a lifetime.

07 sections 6.14/6.15; list traced without scoring.; Source wording: Why mixed precision: precision is a resource, like energy or wiring length; in an A-Life setting, where many organisms must run in parallel on modest hardware, allocating precision well is the difference between a population of ten and a population of ten thousand.

07 sections 6.14/6.15; list traced without scoring.; Source wording: MACRO: organism brain (arbiter + world model + homeostasis) — contains the meso cells below; any cell may itself contain a full sub-brain.

07 sections 6.14/6.15; list traced without scoring.; Source wording: NESTOR treats numeric format as a per-tensor, per-role, per-time decision; the ladder runs from noisy analog and event codes at the bottom to FP64 and beyond at the top; 'bits' are per stored value, excluding shared scale metadata where block formats apply. Default zones: bulk micro weights, activations and signals, meso compute, slow error-intolerant macro state; the modifiers cut across rungs; the adaptive allocator moves tensors up and down the ladder at run time.

07 sections 6.14/6.15; list traced without scoring.; Source wording: Precision ladder rung 3 of 21 (1 = bottom: cheaper, denser; 21 = top: more bits, range, fidelity): Stochastic bitstream — value = probability of a 1; precision grows with stream length.

07 sections 6.14/6.15; list traced without scoring.; Source wording: Principle: precision follows sensitivity times lifetime. A tensor deserves more bits when (a) the organism's behaviour is sensitive to small errors in it and (b) those errors accumulate over its lifetime instead of being washed out.

07 sections 6.14/6.15; list traced without scoring.; Source wording: Precision demand D(theta) = E[ ||grad_theta L|| ] * sigma_q(theta) [first-order sensitivity] x T_life(theta) / tau_wash(theta) [accumulation], where sigma_q is the quantisation noise at the current rung, T_life is how long the value persists, and tau_wash is how fast downstream dynamics forget perturbations; L may be a task loss, a homeostatic error, or divergence of behaviour from a high-precision shadow run.

07 sections 6.14/6.15; list traced without scoring.; Source wording: Static default 1: Bulk micro weights (sensory reservoirs, spiking motifs): ternary to INT4. Their errors are averaged over many synapses.
07 sections 6.14/6.15; list traced without scoring.; Source wording: Static default 2: Activations and spike/state traffic: INT8 or FP8 E4M3; E5M2 for gradients and rarely large signals.

07 sections 6.14/6.15; list traced without scoring.; Source wording: Static default 3: Time constants, gates, leak rates, LTC tau parameters: FP32. Small errors in tau shift the whole dynamical regime.

07 sections 6.14/6.15; list traced without scoring.; Source wording: Static default 4: Accumulators (membrane potentials over long windows, eligibility traces, reward integrals): FP32 or posit32, with stochastic rounding if stored lower.
07 sections 6.14/6.15; list traced without scoring.; Source wording: Static default 5: Homeostatic set points and slow integrators: FP64. These are few, long-lived and drift-sensitive.
07 sections 6.14/6.15; list traced without scoring.; Source wording: Static default 6: Master copies for self-rewrite: FP32 shadow of any weight that the governor may modify (Section 6).

07 sections 6.14/6.15; list traced without scoring.; Source wording: Adaptive precision trigger 1 (precision moves at run time): Shadow divergence: periodically run a cell at one rung higher on the same input and measure behavioural divergence; promote if divergence exceeds a budget, demote if it stays negligible.

07 sections 6.14/6.15; list traced without scoring.; Source wording: Adaptive precision trigger 2 (precision moves at run time): Surprise: when a cell's prediction error spikes (novel environment, injury), temporarily promote its precision so learning is not swamped by quantisation noise; demote as surprise decays.

07 sections 6.14/6.15; list traced without scoring.; Source wording: Adaptive precision trigger 3 (precision moves at run time): Energy budget: an organism-level energy variable (itself a causal part of the simulation) caps total bit-operations; the allocator solves a knapsack-like problem, maximising sum D(theta) * benefit subject to cost.

07 sections 6.14/6.15; list traced without scoring.; Source wording: A useful developmental schedule (Recipe R8) starts the organism at high precision and anneals toward lower precision as structure stabilises, the reverse of the usual train-then-quantise pipeline.

07 sections 6.14/6.15; list traced without scoring.; Source wording: sLTC as the flagship micro/meso block: the default choice for any sub-brain that is event-driven, energy-limited or a candidate for low precision; NESTOR-specific hypotheses (untested by the published work): sLTC cells tolerate ternary weights and INT8 state, their spikes are a natural S2S payload, and banks of sLTC cells with similar time constants are good DSD targets.

07 sections 6.14/6.15; list traced without scoring.; Source wording: Allocation can be fixed by the designer, chosen by evolution (the model type is a gene), or learned by a router that instantiates candidate families in parallel and lets DSD merge the winners.

07 sections 6.14/6.15; list traced without scoring.; Source wording: Interfaces: every port is typed by (algebra, shape, precision, clock, semantics tag); spikes, continuous states, latent caches and scalar neuromodulators are all legal port types; text tokens are not required anywhere.

07 sections 6.14/6.15; list traced without scoring.; Source wording: Shared state (ii): global neuromodulators — a handful of FP32/FP64 scalars, e.g. 'arousal', 'reward prediction error', 'fatigue' — that multiply gains and plasticity rates everywhere.

07 sections 6.14/6.15; list traced without scoring.; Source wording: Timescales: each cell runs on its own clock: fixed-step, event-driven, or adaptive-step (ODE solver). The runtime is a multi-rate scheduler: fast cells take many steps per slow step; slow cells see fast cells through time-aggregating adapters (rate, last value, leaky average, or a learned summariser); fast cells see slow cells as piecewise-constant or interpolated context.; Source criterion: Communication across a timescale boundary is always mediated, never a raw read of another cell's internal buffer.

07 sections 6.14/6.15; list traced without scoring.; Source wording: Differential weights and biases: each weight may be stored as a base value plus differentials, w = w0 + dw(position) + dw(context) + dw(time); the base w0 can be shared across many synapses by DSD, while the small differentials are stored at low precision.

07 sections 6.14/6.15; list traced without scoring.; Source wording: Placement manifold / differential spacing: every cell and unit has coordinates in a placement space (a 3D body frame, a sphere S2 or hypersphere, or a hyperbolic disc); wiring probability, conduction delay and plasticity rate are functions of placement distance — spacing is not cosmetic layout but a parameter that changes delays and coupling.

07 sections 6.14/6.15; list traced without scoring.; Source wording: S2S precision mismatch rule (1): decode with the source's scale metadata (block scales, zero points) before projecting; never project raw integer codes.

07 sections 6.14/6.15; list traced without scoring.; Source wording: S2S precision mismatch rule (2): project in an interchange precision at least as high as the higher of the two endpoints, BF16 by default and FP32 for channels into slow integrators.

07 sections 6.14/6.15; list traced without scoring.; Source wording: S2S precision mismatch rule (3): re-quantise into the target's format with stochastic rounding so that repeated small updates are not rounded away.

07 sections 6.14/6.15; list traced without scoring.; Source wording: S2S precision mismatch rule (4): monitor the channel's precision loss, the divergence between the fused result at interchange precision and at target precision, and let the allocator promote the channel if it is large.

07 sections 6.14/6.15; list traced without scoring.; Source wording: S2S timescale mismatch rule 1: Fast to slow: aggregate (spike counts, exponential traces with time constant matched to the target, or a tiny learned summariser). Aliasing is the main risk; low-pass before downsampling.

07 sections 6.14/6.15; list traced without scoring.; Source wording: S2S timescale mismatch rule 3: Event-driven: send only when the source state changes by more than a threshold (delta coding), which also makes the channel sparse and cheap.

07 sections 6.14/6.15; list traced without scoring.; Source wording: ChronoBlock-4 (CB4): a block-scaled 4-bit format with a temporal (spike-count) precision channel and a geometric grade map. A tensor is cut into blocks of 16 elements; each block stores a shared FP8 (E4M3) scale s_b, as in NVFP4, and a 2-bit mode tag mu_b; 16 element codes of 4 bits each; plus one tensor-level FP32 scale S.

07 sections 6.14/6.15; list traced without scoring.; Source wording: CB4 element codes are interpreted according to the mode tag: FP4 mode (E2M1, as NVFP4); ternary-plus-time mode (2 bits ternary q in {-1, 0, +1} and a 2-bit temporal dither phase); grade mode (the 64 element bits are reallocated across two Cl(3,0) multivectors, e.g. scalar 6, each vector component 4, each bivector component 3, trivector 2 bits, totalling 58 bits plus spare).

07 sections 6.14/6.15; list traced without scoring.; Source wording: CB4 decoded value of element i at time step t: x_i(t) = S * s_b * ( q_i + eps_b [ b_i(t) - 1/2 ] ), b_i(t) = 1[ (t + phi_i) mod L < r_i ], where q_i is the stored code, eps_b one unit in the last place for the block, phi_i the stored dither phase, r_i a residual rate; over an integration window of L steps the time average recovers sub-ULP resolution: precision grows with integration time, so a cell receives a 4-bit value per step but effectively more bits per window.

07 sections 6.14/6.15; list traced without scoring.; Source wording: CB4 storage is 4 + (8 + 2)/16 ~ 4.63 bits per element, plus a negligible tensor scale, versus about 4.5 for NVFP4; the allocator flips one 2-bit tag per block, so adaptive precision costs no data movement.

07 sections 6.14/6.15; list traced without scoring.; Source wording: CB4 cost: decoding needs a mode switch and a phase counter per block; on current hardware this would be emulated (no native support), so speed claims must be measured on custom kernels, FPGAs or neuromorphic hardware.; Source criterion: Specialist test (E11b): emulate CB4 against NVFP4, MXFP4, INT4 and ternary at matched bits per element on (i) weight storage of an sLTC network, (ii) multivector weights in a rotation task; measure accuracy versus integration window L and drift of slow integrators.

07 sections 6.14/6.15; list traced without scoring.; Source wording: Spindle synapse cost per synapse: a pointer (12–16 bits for a library of 4k–64k rotors) plus a 3-component bivector at about 4 bits each, i.e. roughly 24–28 bits per synapse for a full 3D rotation and gain, with the distance computed from positions (cacheable); with CB4 storage, the differential lives in grade mode at 3–4 bits per component; the sandwich product costs on the order of tens of multiply–adds.

07 sections 6.14/6.15; list traced without scoring.; Source wording: Spindle synapse: W_ij = g(d_H(p_i, p_j)) R_cij exp(-delta_ij/2), g(d) = exp(-d/lambda); delay dt_ij = d_H(p_i, p_j) / v_c — each synapse rotates a multivector signal, attenuates it by hyperbolic distance, and delays it by distance.

07 sections 6.14/6.15; list traced without scoring.; Source wording: Design principle P3. Omnitemporal. 07 sections 6.14/6.15; list traced without scoring.; Source wording: Design principle P4. Omnimodal. 07 sections 6.14/6.15; list traced without scoring.; Source wording: Design principle P5. Multiplatform. 07 sections 6.14/6.15; list traced without scoring.; Source wording: Design principle P7. Reversible structure. Every structural operation (unfold, merge, rewrite, precision change) is logged with enough information to undo it.
